So, I have been taken up on performing the task of GMing for Rise of the Runelords.

I have noticed that with a little bit of wiggle room, the main antagonist "Nualia" can be used to make my parties Paladin tear his hair out with a massive dilemma. Which involves her living, where the module has pre-ordained her to die.

Now of course, this "Xanatos Gambit" would be great in the short term, for the first book, but I'm not so sure how her living would affect the rest of the module, since I would totally have her re-occurring, if the PCs take her on the offer to save the town (Somewhat, I think I have made a situation where Sandpoint is screwed either way)

Have any of you GMs ever taken a module, and radically change what would happen? How did you find that interacted with the rest of the module? As a player, have you ever seen a module that you knew, and watch the GM explicitly go off the rails of the module, and what did you think?
Rise of the Runelords, book 1 - a discussion, and running modules.

Well, in my game, the PCs were forced to leave Thistletop due to remaining health points and an actual party death, so they defeated Nualia but did not finish the job. I basically curved this by running a short dungeon where they would meet those that were not taken care of at intervals (being Nualia, Ripnugget, and, unfortunately for them, Malfeshnekor) in a side dungeon.

You can curb the course with a bit of intricate writing while also staying on track, or simply use Nualia at a much later time to fill in as someone they will either regret not having killed or as some sort of figurehead. It is almost impossible to not have a player alter the course of destiny, so just go with the flow.
